title: The World of Time and Responsibility

missions.title: The Treasure Called Time

ayahs.arabic: وَالعَصرِ
إِنَّ الإِنسـٰنَ لَفى خُسرٍ
إِلَّا الَّذينَ ءامَنوا وَعَمِلُوا الصّـٰلِحـٰتِ وَتَواصَوا بِالحَقِّ وَتَواصَوا بِالصَّبرِ

options: Count yourself a failure because one task was missed.
Remember faith, good actions, truth and patience while adjusting the plan.
Ignore all your responsibilities because plans sometimes change.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 103:1, 103:2, 103:3   |   CORE VALUES: Īmān • Righteous deeds • Truth • Patience
missions.aim: Learn that Surah Al-‘Asr links our precious time to faith, good actions, mutual truthfulness and patient encouragement.
missions.meaning: Allah swears by time and warns of human loss, except for people who believe, do righteous deeds, advise one another toward truth, and advise one another toward patience.
missions.tafsir: Surah Al-‘Asr is short but gathers the foundations of a purposeful life. Al-‘Asr is time, during which people make choices that carry consequences. The exception to loss has four connected parts: belief, righteous action, mutual counsel toward the truth, and mutual counsel toward patience. Ibn Kathir explains that belief must be joined with deeds and that advising one another requires goodness and perseverance. Children should not be taught that every minute needs measurable output. Time also includes rest, play, family and growing up. The point is to choose what is right and not lose sight of Allah. In our story, a daily plan becomes a gentle reminder, not an instrument for shaming children about productivity. The first three verses are displayed in full and memorized progressively.
missions.story: Akhlaq found an empty page in his new notebook and announced, “Today I will fill every minute with achievements!” He wrote down homework, drawing, football, reading, helping Salamah, and three more tasks. After lunch, he was upset because everything had not fitted into the day. Imaan brought him a glass of water and asked him to think about Surah Al-‘Asr. “Did you speak truthfully? Did you help someone? Were you patient when your plan changed?” Akhlaq remembered that he had encouraged Mohsin when a drawing went wrong. The page was not full, but his day had contained good. Together, they drew a simple plan with time for prayer, effort, play, and rest.
missions.question: Your day did not go exactly as planned. What matters most?
missions.feedback: Surah Al-‘Asr guides the kind of life we seek, not a competition to fill every moment.
missions.action: Choose one good deed today and complete it patiently.
missions.reflection: How did I use one moment today to choose what was right?
missions.careNote: Never use screen-time streaks, productivity scores or fear-of-loss imagery to pressure children.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: When One Task Is Finished

ayahs.arabic: فَإِذا فَرَغتَ فَانصَب
وَإِلىٰ رَبِّكَ فَارغَب

options: Check the next responsibility and make time for remembering Allah.
Start ten new tasks without resting or praying.
Assume all promises for the day no longer matter.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 94:7, 94:8   |   CORE VALUES: Worship • Purpose • Turning to Allah
missions.aim: Understand that completing one responsibility is an opportunity to turn sincerely toward Allah, not to chase endless busyness.
missions.meaning: After finishing, devote yourself earnestly, and turn your longing and hope to your Lord.
missions.tafsir: The final verses of Ash-Sharh direct the Prophet ﷺ to renew earnest devotion when free from one occupation and to turn his desire toward Allah. Exegetes discuss the relation between finishing duties and giving oneself to worship and supplication. The passage is not an instruction that children must be working all the time, nor a rule that rest is wrong. Its teaching is about purposeful turning toward Allah and resisting aimless neglect of what matters. The previous verses of the surah speak of relief with difficulty and Allah’s care, so hope belongs in our lesson. A child can finish homework, thank Allah, and prepare calmly for Salah or another responsible activity. We keep the divine address and its context separate from the fictional modern example.
missions.story: Imaan finished a school project much earlier than expected. She opened a game and almost forgot that she had promised to help Dadi Jaan arrange some books. When Salamah reminded her, she closed the game and went to Dadi Jaan. They arranged the books together, then paused for Asr prayer. Dadi Jaan explained that completing a task gives us a chance to turn our attention toward something worthwhile, especially remembering Allah. Imaan still enjoyed her game later. She discovered that choosing the next good thing did not mean losing every moment of fun; it meant caring about what came next.
missions.question: You complete your assignment. What is a thoughtful next step?
missions.feedback: A thoughtful next step can be worship, helping, needed rest or an agreed responsibility.
missions.action: After finishing one task, pause and consciously remember Allah before choosing what comes next.
missions.reflection: What usually happens when I finish something important?
missions.vocabulary: Faraghta — you have finished; Fansab — strive/devote yourself; Farghab — turn your longing
missions.careNote: Do not present an endless-work ethic; child needs rest and play.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: The Blessing of Rest

ayahs.arabic: وَجَعَلنا نَومَكُم سُباتًا
وَجَعَلنَا الَّيلَ لِباسًا
وَجَعَلنَا النَّهارَ مَعاشًا

options: Pretend you need no rest and stay awake even longer.
Talk to a caregiver and make a calmer routine with enough rest.
Blame everyone else for your tiredness.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 78:9, 78:10, 78:11   |   CORE VALUES: Sleep • Balance • Grateful routine
missions.aim: Appreciate sleep, night and daytime as Allah’s provisions and form a healthy, flexible routine.
missions.meaning: Allah describes sleep as rest, night as a covering, and daytime as a time for livelihood and activity.
missions.tafsir: In Surah An-Naba’, Allah calls attention to familiar signs of His power: sleep, the covering of night, and the daylight in which people pursue their needs. These are blessings and signs for reflection. The verses do not prescribe a universal bedtime or declare that every person has identical schedules. For a child, the lesson is to appreciate rest and to use active hours constructively. A balanced routine supports attention, kindness and worship. We should not turn Qur’anic verses into a medical sleep chart or blame children with disabilities, sleep disorders, illness or unusual family routines. The story simply helps children notice that Allah made our days with rhythms and opportunities.
missions.story: Akhlaq stayed awake late building a paper city. The next morning, even his favorite breakfast felt uninteresting. He snapped when Imaan asked to borrow a ruler. Salaam helped him see that being tired can make ordinary things difficult. That evening, the family planned a calmer routine. Akhlaq would keep his supplies in one basket, finish the paper city over several days, and ask for support when he was restless. Imaan chose a bedtime story. They thought about how night brings rest and the day brings chances to learn, worship and play. Akhlaq apologized for speaking sharply and went to bed without feeling that the unfinished city was a failure.
missions.question: You are tired after staying up late. What is wise?
missions.feedback: Rest is a blessing, and a gentle routine helps us care for the people around us.
missions.action: With a caregiver, prepare one simple bedtime step tonight.
missions.reflection: What helps me feel rested and ready to be kind?
missions.vocabulary: Subāt — repose/rest; Libās — covering; Ma‘āsh — livelihood
missions.careNote: Do not give medical advice or punish irregular sleep; support diverse needs.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: When It Is Time for Jumu‘ah

ayahs.arabic: يـٰأَيُّهَا الَّذينَ ءامَنوا إِذا نودِىَ لِلصَّلوٰةِ مِن يَومِ الجُمُعَةِ فَاسعَوا إِلىٰ ذِكرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا البَيعَ ۚ ذٰلِكُم خَيرٌ لَكُم إِن كُنتُم تَعلَمونَ
فَإِذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلوٰةُ فَانتَشِروا فِى الأَرضِ وَابتَغوا مِن فَضلِ اللَّهِ وَاذكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثيرًا لَعَلَّكُم تُفلِحونَ

options: Make loud jokes during the khutbah.
Follow family guidance and prepare calmly for worship.
Say that anyone not attending must be a bad Muslim.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 62:9, 62:10   |   CORE VALUES: Worship priorities • Community • Balance
missions.aim: Understand the Qur’anic priority of Friday congregational prayer for those responsible for it, and the balance between worship and lawful work.
missions.meaning: When the call to Friday prayer is made, those addressed are to proceed to Allah’s remembrance and leave trade; after prayer, they may go about their affairs, seek Allah’s bounty and remember Him.
missions.tafsir: Surah Al-Jumu‘ah teaches believers to prioritize the Friday congregational prayer when its call is made and to leave business transactions at that time. The following verse allows believers to spread out afterward, seek Allah’s bounty and remember Him often. This teaches that worship has rightful priority while work itself is not condemned. The obligation of Jumu‘ah applies according to established legal conditions; young children are learning and should not be presented as bearing the same duties as accountable adults. Families should guide their child’s mosque participation and local practice. The focus is joyful preparation and respect for worship, not criticizing those with legitimate exemptions. Other school-of-law details remain in caregiver-facing notes.
missions.story: On Friday morning, Akhlaq wanted to continue a marketplace game just as Salaam was preparing to go to the mosque. Salaam explained that a Muslim should be ready for Jumu‘ah rather than be distracted by trade or entertainment at the prayer time. Akhlaq was still young, but he wanted to learn. He helped find a clean prayer cap and asked what to do respectfully during the khutbah. Imaan planned a quiet reading activity with Salamah. Later the family gathered for lunch and resumed their ordinary tasks. Akhlaq noticed that prayer had a special place in the day, yet the day also held work, rest and kindness.
missions.question: Your family is preparing for Jumu‘ah. How can you learn respectfully?
missions.feedback: Learn the importance of Jumu‘ah while respecting different ages, circumstances and lawful exemptions.
missions.action: Ask a caregiver one question about the etiquette of Jumu‘ah and practise the answer.
missions.reflection: How can I show respect when other people are worshipping?
missions.vocabulary: Jumu‘ah — Friday congregational prayer; Dhikr — remembrance; Faḍl — bounty
missions.careNote: Explicitly note legal exemptions and differing family circumstances; no compulsory attendance claims for small children.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Salah Has an Appointed Time

ayahs.arabic: فَإِذا قَضَيتُمُ الصَّلوٰةَ فَاذكُرُوا اللَّهَ قِيـٰمًا وَقُعودًا وَعَلىٰ جُنوبِكُم ۚ فَإِذَا اطمَأنَنتُم فَأَقيمُوا الصَّلوٰةَ ۚ إِنَّ الصَّلوٰةَ كانَت عَلَى المُؤمِنينَ كِتـٰبًا مَوقوتًا

options: Learn the prayer time and follow your caregiver’s guidance.
Ignore prayer reminders forever because games are more fun.
Tell another child that missing a practice session makes them worthless.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 4:103   |   CORE VALUES: Prayer awareness • Routine • Responsibility
missions.aim: Recognize that Salah is prescribed at appointed times and that prayer deserves a caring place in one’s day.
missions.meaning: After the instruction about prayer amid particular circumstances, the verse emphasizes remembering Allah and that prayer is prescribed for believers at appointed times.
missions.tafsir: The verse appears in the context of prayer under conditions of danger and the return to security. It speaks of remembering Allah in different positions and establishing prayer properly once safe, then states that prayer is prescribed for believers at appointed times. This last clause is central to our child-friendly mission, but the full verse and its preceding context must remain available. Children develop responsibility gradually under the care of parents and teachers. A gentle routine, rather than surveillance, can help them recognize the right times and prepare for Salah. The app must not pronounce legal judgments about a child’s obligation or use spiritual fear to induce compliance. The exact prayer-time calculation belongs to a separate verified feature, not an imaginary story timer.
missions.story: Imaan and Akhlaq were building a bridge from wooden blocks when the prayer reminder sounded in their home. Akhlaq asked whether he could simply guess the time later. Salaam sat beside him and explained that the daily prayers have appointed times and that learning to notice them is part of growing in worship. They placed the blocks carefully to one side. After prayer, they returned to the bridge and discovered it was still standing. Imaan drew small pictures of the day’s five prayers for a family chart, with room for questions rather than angry marks. Akhlaq enjoyed finding out why the schedule mattered.
missions.question: Your family’s prayer time has arrived while you are playing. What can you do?
missions.feedback: Learning Salah is a steady journey; routines help us honour its appointed time.
missions.action: With your caregiver, identify the next Salah time and prepare calmly for it.
missions.reflection: What small habit helps me remember prayer without feeling rushed?
missions.vocabulary: Ṣalāh — prayer; Mawqūt — appointed in time; Dhikr — remembrance
missions.careNote: Religious obligations and clock times require jurisprudential and local-calendar validation; never shame children.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Protecting Our Attention

ayahs.arabic: قَد أَفلَحَ المُؤمِنونَ
الَّذينَ هُم فى صَلاتِهِم خـٰشِعونَ
وَالَّذينَ هُم عَنِ اللَّغوِ مُعرِضونَ

options: Keep interrupting because your joke is funny.
Give them space and save the joke for a suitable time.
Say that all laughter is forbidden.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 23:1, 23:2, 23:3   |   CORE VALUES: Salah focus • Leaving idle distractions • Inner calm
missions.aim: Learn that successful believers combine reverence in Salah with turning away from useless or harmful talk.
missions.meaning: The opening of Surah Al-Mu’minun describes successful believers as humble and attentive in prayer, and as people who turn away from idle or pointless matters.
missions.tafsir: The first verses of Al-Mu’minun describe the success of believers and mention khushū‘ in prayer—reverent humility before Allah—and their turning away from laghw, idle or blameworthy talk and conduct. Scholarly explanations emphasize prayer of the heart as well as bodily conduct. Khushū‘ is not a game score. Children naturally learn focus gradually, and their minds may wander. Gentle modelling, a calm prayer environment and simple explanations are better than scolding them for distraction. Laghw should not be falsely equated with all play, art or laughter. Rather, our application encourages choosing activities and words with wisdom and avoiding harmful chatter that wastes others’ attention or causes discomfort.
missions.story: During an afternoon activity, Akhlaq kept sending funny sounds across the table while Imaan was trying to finish a reading challenge. Everyone laughed at first, but then Mohsina asked for a little quiet. Akhlaq noticed that a joke can stop being helpful when it disturbs another person. He apologized and suggested a five-minute play break after the task. Later, in Salah practice, he learned that focusing on Allah takes patience too. When his thoughts wandered, Salaam encouraged him to try again calmly rather than become embarrassed. Imaan learned that being serious at the right time and cheerful at the right time both require thoughtfulness.
missions.question: Your friend is trying to concentrate. What should you do?
missions.feedback: Protecting attention means being considerate—not giving up healthy play.
missions.action: Give someone ten uninterrupted minutes to finish a task or worship.
missions.reflection: When is quietness a form of kindness?
missions.vocabulary: Khushū‘ — reverent humility; Laghw — idle or vain matters; Aflaha — succeeded
missions.careNote: No claim that the game can assess sincerity or prayer quality; accommodate neurodiversity.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Remember to Say In Shaa Allah

ayahs.arabic: وَلا تَقولَنَّ لِشَا۟ىءٍ إِنّى فاعِلٌ ذٰلِكَ غَدًا
إِلّا أَن يَشاءَ اللَّهُ ۚ وَاذكُر رَبَّكَ إِذا نَسيتَ وَقُل عَسىٰ أَن يَهدِيَنِ رَبّى لِأَقرَبَ مِن هـٰذا رَشَدًا

options: Say In Shaa Allah and make a real effort to remember.
Say In Shaa Allah so you never need to try.
Guarantee tomorrow will happen exactly as you want.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 18:23, 18:24   |   CORE VALUES: Humility • Planning • Reliance on Allah
missions.aim: Understand that future plans depend on Allah’s will and that saying In Shaa Allah should accompany sincere effort.
missions.meaning: Allah teaches not to speak with certainty about what one will do tomorrow without connecting it to Allah’s will; remember Allah when you forget and ask for guidance.
missions.tafsir: These verses teach that future events belong to Allah’s knowledge and will. In the context of the Prophet’s ﷺ promise to answer questions, the Qur’an instructs remembering Allah and saying In Shaa Allah concerning what one intends to do in the future. This is a lesson in humility, not a magic guarantee that every plan will succeed. Nor should children use the phrase as an excuse for making a promise they do not intend to keep. The verses also teach remembrance if one forgets and seeking guidance from the Lord. Because the full context is part of Surah Al-Kahf, the app should cross-link to our earlier Kahf volume rather than presenting the phrase as an isolated slogan.
missions.story: Akhlaq told Mohsin, “I will definitely bring the model spaceship tomorrow!” Imaan smiled and reminded him that we say In Shaa Allah about plans for the future. “Does that mean I can forget it?” Akhlaq asked. “No,” Imaan replied. “We still try our best.” That evening, Akhlaq put the spaceship beside his schoolbag and asked Salaam for help keeping it safe. The next day, rain delayed the journey, and Mohsin could not collect it. Akhlaq felt disappointed, but understood that not every detail is in his control. He made a new plan politely and did not pretend that the original promise had never mattered.
missions.question: You promise to bring a book tomorrow. What is the responsible response?
missions.feedback: Reliance on Allah goes together with honest intention and practical preparation.
missions.action: For one plan tomorrow, say In Shaa Allah and take one real preparation step.
missions.reflection: What part of my plan is my responsibility, and what is beyond my control?
missions.vocabulary: In shā’a Allāh — if Allah wills; Rashad — right guidance; Dhikr — remembrance
missions.careNote: Do not label a child sinful for forgetting a phrase; teach calmly. Avoid forecasting outcomes.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: A Promise Is a Responsibility

ayahs.arabic: وَلا تَقرَبوا مالَ اليَتيمِ إِلّا بِالَّتى هِىَ أَحسَنُ حَتّىٰ يَبلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ ۚ وَأَوفوا بِالعَهدِ ۖ إِنَّ العَهدَ كانَ مَسـٔولًا

options: Hide it and hope the owner forgets.
Explain honestly, care for it and arrange a new return time.
Pass it to someone else without asking.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 17:34   |   CORE VALUES: Trusts • Promises • Protecting rights
missions.aim: Understand that the Qur’an demands protection of vulnerable people’s property and fulfilment of commitments.
missions.meaning: Allah forbids approaching an orphan’s property except in the best way until maturity, and commands fulfilment of commitments because every commitment will be questioned.
missions.tafsir: Al-Isra 17:34 begins with an instruction to safeguard the property of an orphan and only handle it in the best way until the orphan reaches maturity. It then commands fulfilment of the covenant, because promises carry accountability. We must not erase the first half of the verse simply to teach timeliness. The guardian’s duty to protect property is substantial; children can understand the smaller analogy of safeguarding things entrusted to them, without imagining themselves responsible for legal guardianship. Keeping promises also requires care: we should not encourage children to fulfil unsafe or improper promises; instead, they should seek adult help and explain honestly if plans must change. Faithfulness is a form of respect for others’ rights.
missions.story: Dadi Jaan lent Akhlaq a small illustrated book, asking him to return it on Saturday. Akhlaq placed it beneath his art supplies and forgot until Saturday morning. He had not finished reading it. Imaan suggested hiding it until next week, but Akhlaq knew he had agreed to a date. He cleaned the cover gently, returned it, and explained what happened. Dadi Jaan appreciated his honesty and offered to lend it again after her own reading time. Salaam used the moment to explain that the Qur’an also protects the rights and property of vulnerable people. A promise is more than a calendar note; it tells another person that their rights matter.
missions.question: You borrowed something and cannot return it when promised. What should you do?
missions.feedback: Respecting agreements means protecting belongings and communicating truthfully.
missions.action: Return one borrowed item or confirm its agreed return time.
missions.reflection: How does keeping a promise show respect?
missions.careNote: Never insist that unsafe promises be fulfilled. Show that property guardianship is an adult legal duty.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Patience and Prayer Together

ayahs.arabic: يـٰأَيُّهَا الَّذينَ ءامَنُوا استَعينوا بِالصَّبرِ وَالصَّلوٰةِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصّـٰبِرينَ

options: Give up immediately and insult the task.
Pray, stay patient, try another method and ask for help when needed.
Hide the problem so no one can help.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 2:153   |   CORE VALUES: Ṣabr • Salah • Seeking help
missions.aim: Learn that the Qur’an directs believers to seek Allah’s help through patience and Salah during difficulty.
missions.meaning: Believers are told to seek help through patience and prayer; Allah is with those who are patient.
missions.tafsir: Al-Baqarah 2:153 joins ṣabr and Salah as means of seeking help from Allah. Patience is not simply keeping silent in pain; it includes steadiness in what is right, avoiding wrongdoing, and continuing with the lawful steps needed to address a problem. Salah connects the believer to Allah, while practical support from family, teachers and trusted adults remains important. The divine promise of Allah’s support must not be turned into a guarantee that homework will become easy or illness will disappear immediately. For young learners, patience can mean attempting a difficult task again, asking for help and not lashing out at others. A short example can show how worship and responsibility reinforce, rather than replace, one another.
missions.story: Mohsin struggled with a difficult maths problem. Akhlaq solved it quickly and almost said, “It is easy!” Imaan noticed Mohsin’s frustration. She remembered the lesson about patience and asked whether he wanted to work through the problem one step at a time. After a family prayer break, Mohsin returned and tried another method with Salaam’s guidance. The answer did not appear instantly, but his understanding grew. Akhlaq apologized for rushing him. Together they learned that patience is not the absence of difficulty; it is a way of responding to difficulty while seeking Allah’s help and accepting appropriate human support.
missions.question: You are stuck on something important. What should you do?
missions.feedback: Seeking Allah’s help includes patient effort and reaching out to trusted people.
missions.action: Try one difficult task calmly for five minutes, then ask for help if needed.
missions.reflection: What helps me remain gentle when a task becomes difficult?
missions.vocabulary: Ṣabr — patience/steadfastness; Ista‘īnū — seek help; Ṣalāh — prayer
missions.careNote: Never use “be patient” to discourage reporting bullying, abuse, illness or injury.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Staying Steadfast

ayahs.arabic: يـٰأَيُّهَا الَّذينَ ءامَنُوا اصبِروا وَصابِروا وَرابِطوا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُم تُفلِحونَ

options: Blame the slowest person.
Encourage one another and revise the plan patiently.
Refuse any help and demand immediate success.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 3:200   |   CORE VALUES: Perseverance • Mutual support • Taqwa
missions.aim: Discover that believers are urged to persevere, encourage one another in steadfastness, and remain mindful of Allah.
missions.meaning: Believers are directed to be patient, strengthen one another in patience, remain firm, and have Taqwa so they may succeed.
missions.tafsir: The closing verse of Ali ‘Imran includes multiple commands: be patient, reinforce patience with one another, maintain readiness and steadfastness, and fear Allah with reverent awareness. Classical commentary takes these words seriously in the life of the believing community, including difficult circumstances and duties. The child-level application emphasizes perseverance, mutual encouragement, and Taqwa while preserving the wider meaning for older readers and teachers. It is not a command to endure abuse or continue unsafe activities. Patience should be guided by wisdom, safety and lawful responsibilities. In the app, children learn that being steadfast may mean finishing an appropriate task with help or being a supportive friend to someone struggling.
missions.story: Amanpur’s class was practising a cooperative puzzle. After two unsuccessful attempts, Akhlaq wanted to leave. Imaan said, “We can try again, but perhaps we need another idea.” Their teacher helped the group divide the work: one learner sorted colours, another checked shapes, and a third offered encouraging words. They completed most of the puzzle before the lesson ended. Instead of feeling defeated, they saved their work and agreed to finish it another time. Akhlaq realized that perseverance can be shared. It was not about forcing everyone to work without rest; it was about facing a good task with patience, cooperation and respect.
missions.question: Your team is struggling with a safe and worthwhile challenge. What helps?
missions.feedback: Steadfastness grows through patience, wisdom and mutual support.
missions.action: Encourage one person who is working hard at a worthwhile task.
missions.reflection: What words help someone persevere without making them feel pressured?
missions.vocabulary: Ṣābirū — persevere together; Rābiṭū — remain steadfast/prepared; Taqwā — God-consciousness
missions.careNote: Never advise children to endure danger or bullying for the sake of patience.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Eager to Do Good

ayahs.arabic: فَاستَجَبنا لَهُ وَوَهَبنا لَهُ يَحيىٰ وَأَصلَحنا لَهُ زَوجَهُ ۚ إِنَّهُم كانوا يُسـٰرِعونَ فِى الخَيرٰتِ وَيَدعونَنا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا ۖ وَكانوا لَنا خـٰشِعينَ

options: Offer help promptly and humbly.
Wait only so you can be praised afterward.
Rush into an unsafe task without asking an adult.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 21:90   |   CORE VALUES: Eagerness for good • Hope • Humility
missions.aim: Recognize that Allah praises people who hasten to good deeds and call upon Him with hope, awe and humility.
missions.meaning: In the account of Zakariyya and his family, Allah describes them as quick in good deeds and supplicating with hope and awe, humble before Him.
missions.tafsir: Surah Al-Anbiya 21:90 describes Allah’s acceptance of the supplication of Prophet Zakariyya and His mercy toward his family, then praises their hastening toward good works, their supplication with hope and awe, and their humility. We must preserve the account’s setting and avoid telling children that performing a challenge guarantees the same specific family outcome. The child-friendly lesson focuses on the praised qualities: promptness in doing what is right, prayer, and humility before Allah. Hurrying to do good does not mean acting recklessly; children should consider safety, consent and parental guidance. It can mean offering help without waiting to be applauded, or responding respectfully when a family duty needs attention.
missions.story: Salamah asked who could help carry light books to the family shelf. Akhlaq thought about waiting until Imaan volunteered. Imaan had already started arranging a space for them. Then Akhlaq remembered the Qur’anic praise for those who hurry toward good deeds. “I can help,” he said, and carried a small stack carefully. When the work was done, he wanted to announce that he had been first. Salaam reminded him that humility matters alongside eagerness. Akhlaq smiled and said, “I’m glad the shelf is ready.” He noticed that a quick good choice feels especially meaningful when it is done without showing off.
missions.question: You notice a safe opportunity to help. What is a good response?
missions.feedback: Eagerness for good belongs with humility and good judgment.
missions.action: Offer one safe act of help promptly, without seeking public praise.
missions.reflection: Why does doing good humbly feel different from showing off?
missions.vocabulary: Yusāri‘ūn — hasten; Raghaban — in hope; Khashi‘īn — humble
missions.careNote: Explain Zakariyya’s original supplication context; do not promise identical outcomes.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Begin with Yourself

ayahs.arabic: لَهُ مُعَقِّبـٰتٌ مِن بَينِ يَدَيهِ وَمِن خَلفِهِ يَحفَظونَهُ مِن أَمرِ اللَّهِ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُغَيِّرُ ما بِقَومٍ حَتّىٰ يُغَيِّروا ما بِأَنفُسِهِم ۗ وَإِذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِقَومٍ سوءًا فَلا مَرَدَّ لَهُ ۚ وَما لَهُم مِن دونِهِ مِن والٍ

options: Accuse someone else without evidence.
Put them in an agreed place and ask for help organizing them.
Believe every problem is caused by your personal failure.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 13:11   |   CORE VALUES: Personal responsibility • Honest self-review • Trust
missions.aim: Understand that change in people’s condition is related to what they change within themselves, while Allah remains the One who controls outcomes.
missions.meaning: Allah describes angels acting by His command and teaches that He does not change a people’s state until they change what is within themselves; His decree remains sovereign.
missions.tafsir: Ar-Ra‘d 13:11 contains a description of angels guarding by Allah’s command, then a principle about the condition of a people and the change within them. Classical Tafsir connects it with Allah’s justice and with what people do in response to His blessings. We must resist the oversimplified slogan “everyone gets whatever they work for.” Poverty, disability, family hardship and the behavior of others are not proof that a child failed to try or lacked faith. Allah controls results, and people have duties within their actual ability. For an accessible modern application, a child may ask, “What behaviour can I improve today?”—while recognizing that some problems require adults, community help and patience, not individual self-blame.
missions.story: Akhlaq often left his pencils scattered across the floor, then became upset when he could not find them. One day he blamed Imaan for borrowing his things. Imaan gently reminded him that he had not put them away after drawing. With Salaam’s help, Akhlaq chose a small change he could make: placing pencils in a box after each activity. He could not control every interruption or everything that happened at school, but he could care for the supplies entrusted to him. After several days he found his pencils more easily. He thanked Imaan for helping and learned that taking one responsible step is better than blaming everyone around us.
missions.question: You keep losing your pencils because they are scattered. What is a fair first step?
missions.feedback: We can change our own choices while treating hardship and other people with compassion.
missions.action: Improve one small habit that is within your ability today.
missions.reflection: What can I control, and when should I ask others for support?
missions.vocabulary: Yughayyiru — changes; Anfusihim — within themselves; Mu‘aqqibāt — successive angels
missions.careNote: Never blame victims of poverty, illness, neglect or disability; full verse meaning required.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Every Good Effort Matters

ayahs.arabic: مَن عَمِلَ صـٰلِحًا مِن ذَكَرٍ أَو أُنثىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤمِنٌ فَلَنُحيِيَنَّهُ حَيوٰةً طَيِّبَةً ۖ وَلَنَجزِيَنَّهُم أَجرَهُم بِأَحسَنِ ما كانوا يَعمَلونَ

options: Value only the project that gets the loudest applause.
Respect both their efforts and avoid judging worth by gender or popularity.
Say only one gender can do meaningful good.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 16:97   |   CORE VALUES: Faith • Righteous action • Equal dignity
missions.aim: Learn that Allah connects faith and righteous deeds with a good life and reward, speaking equally of men and women.
missions.meaning: Allah promises a good life and fitting reward to any believer—male or female—who does righteous deeds.
missions.tafsir: An-Nahl 16:97 affirms that righteous action joined to faith is honored by Allah whether done by a man or a woman. Explanations of the “good life” include contentment and wholesome living; the verse is not a material prosperity guarantee. A child should not be told that being sick or poor means Allah has rejected their efforts. The gender-inclusive wording is essential and should not be omitted from the app. In children’s life, the application is that honest helpful work matters regardless of whether a boy or a girl performs it and whether anyone applauds. Praise effort with care, but do not pretend an educational algorithm knows the size of reward with Allah.
missions.story: At the Amanpur science fair, Mohsina and Akhlaq worked on separate water-saving projects. Some classmates crowded around Akhlaq’s table because it had colourful moving pieces. Mohsina’s model was simpler but carefully explained how to reduce waste. Imaan visited both tables and thanked each learner for their effort. A teacher reminded the class that good deeds and worthy work are not measured by who receives the loudest applause. Akhlaq asked Mohsina about her design and learned a new idea. By the end, the children felt proud of learning and helping rather than comparing boys and girls or counting how many visitors stopped by.
missions.question: Two classmates work sincerely on useful projects. How should we value them?
missions.feedback: The Qur’an honors righteous effort by believing men and women alike.
missions.action: Recognize one person’s sincere effort without comparing or ranking them.
missions.reflection: Why is public attention a poor measure of a good deed?
missions.vocabulary: ‘Amila ṣāliḥan — did righteous deeds; Ḥayāh ṭayyibah — good life; Ajr — reward
missions.careNote: No spiritual reward scores or prosperity claims; avoid stereotypes about boys and girls.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Day and Night as Opportunities

ayahs.arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذى جَعَلَ الَّيلَ وَالنَّهارَ خِلفَةً لِمَن أَرادَ أَن يَذَّكَّرَ أَو أَرادَ شُكورًا

options: Decide the whole day is worthless.
Choose another useful activity now and try the game when it is safe.
Go outside in dangerous weather to prove you are productive.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 25:62   |   CORE VALUES: Reflection • Gratitude • Flexible routines
missions.aim: Notice that day and night follow one another as opportunities for remembrance and gratitude.
missions.meaning: Allah made night and day succeed one another for those who wish to remember or show gratitude.
missions.tafsir: Al-Furqan 25:62 draws attention to the succession of night and day: those seeking a reminder or gratitude can reflect on this repeated sign. Classical exegesis also explores how the alternation offers opportunities to make up certain good deeds when time passes. A child-focused lesson can invite careful appreciation of a new morning, the quiet of evening, and the fact that missed opportunities can often be approached again with a good intention. This is not a specific ritual imposed at sunrise or sunset, and there is no special point multiplier for studying at night. The verse provides a gentle, hopeful basis for reflection. Families may have different schedules; the app should adapt without claiming one universal routine.
missions.story: It had rained all afternoon, and Akhlaq’s outdoor game was cancelled. He complained that the day had been wasted. At sunset he saw light spreading across the wet garden, and Imaan suggested sketching the clouds. The next morning, they checked whether the playground was dry enough to use. Salaam spoke with them about the way Allah makes night and day follow one another. Yesterday’s cancelled game did not mean every opportunity was gone. Akhlaq enjoyed drawing during the rain and playing safely after it cleared. He began to see that different parts of a day offer different blessings.
missions.question: An outdoor plan is cancelled by rain. What is a balanced choice?
missions.feedback: Night and day each offer opportunities to remember Allah and be grateful.
missions.action: Notice one blessing of the morning or evening and thank Allah for it.
missions.reflection: Which time of day helps me slow down and notice blessings?
missions.vocabulary: Khilfah — succeeding/alternating; Tadhakkur — remembrance; Shukūr — gratitude
missions.careNote: No fixed compulsory routine; avoid unsafe outdoor missions or compulsory geolocation.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: Even the Smallest Deed Counts

ayahs.arabic: يَومَئِذٍ يَصدُرُ النّاسُ أَشتاتًا لِيُرَوا أَعمـٰلَهُم
فَمَن يَعمَل مِثقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيرًا يَرَهُ
وَمَن يَعمَل مِثقالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ

options: Ignore it because small deeds do not matter.
Choose the good action if it is safe and appropriate.
Announce it loudly so you can earn more points.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 99:6, 99:7, 99:8   |   CORE VALUES: Accountability • Small goodness • Careful choices
missions.aim: Understand that Allah’s knowledge includes even the smallest deeds, encouraging sincere good and thoughtful avoidance of wrong.
missions.meaning: People will be shown their deeds; whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of wrong will see it.
missions.tafsir: The closing verses of Az-Zalzalah proclaim accountability: nothing is hidden from Allah, however small the action. This encourages care with minor words and seemingly invisible kindness. The passage also speaks seriously of wrongdoing; it must not be turned into a frightening game where children see ominous punishment animations or are made to obsess over every thought. Theologically, the verses concern the Hereafter, not a school badge system or an algorithm that assigns heavenly rewards. A child may use the teaching to remember that picking up a dropped pencil, admitting a mistake, or refraining from an unkind word matters. At the same time, Allah’s forgiveness and mercy remain vital parts of an age-appropriate conversation.
missions.story: During lunch, Akhlaq noticed a small piece of paper by the classroom door. He almost walked past because it seemed too tiny to matter. Then he picked it up and placed it in the recycling bin. Mohsin thanked him, but no one else noticed. Later, Imaan found that she had interrupted Mohsina while she was speaking. She apologized rather than pretending it had not happened. In their evening discussion, Salaam reminded the children that the Qur’an teaches accountability even for very small actions. They were not keeping a scoreboard of each other’s mistakes; they were learning to choose good, ask forgiveness and appreciate Allah’s mercy.
missions.question: A tiny opportunity to help appears and nobody is watching. What should you do?
missions.feedback: Small deeds count, even when no human audience is watching.
missions.action: Perform one small helpful deed quietly today.
missions.reflection: Which tiny good choice can become a habit?
missions.vocabulary: Mithqāl — weight/measure; Dharrāh — tiny particle; Khayr — good
missions.careNote: No anxiety-inducing reward-and-punishment counters; mention Allah’s mercy alongside accountability.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?

missions.title: The Purpose of Doing Good

ayahs.arabic: الَّذى خَلَقَ المَوتَ وَالحَيوٰةَ لِيَبلُوَكُم أَيُّكُم أَحسَنُ عَمَلًا ۚ وَهُوَ العَزيزُ الغَفورُ

options: Race through many missions without understanding.
Understand the lesson and put one good action into practice.
Keep playing until a large badge number appears.
missions.anchor: FOCUS AYAHS: 67:2   |   CORE VALUES: Life’s purpose • Excellence • Sincerity
missions.aim: Reflect gently that life is a test of the quality and sincerity of our deeds, not a contest of quantity.
missions.meaning: Allah created death and life to test people as to who is best in deeds; He is the Mighty and the Forgiving.
missions.tafsir: Al-Mulk 67:2 teaches that life and death belong to Allah and that human beings are tested in their deeds; Allah is described as the Mighty and Forgiving. The verse emphasizes who is best in deeds rather than who does the greatest number of visible tasks. Exegetes draw attention to the quality and truthfulness of work, including obedience to Allah. Young children should not encounter frightening representations of death or be invited to imagine losing loved ones as part of the game. We can teach the hopeful application that sincere, well-chosen actions matter more than collecting endless digital badges. The original theological teaching about life, death and accountability remains accessible in a parent-guided explanation, while the fictional example centers on intention and responsible behavior.
missions.story: Akhlaq wanted to earn as many virtual flowers as possible in Amanpur’s learning garden. He clicked through activities quickly without reading the stories. Imaan noticed that he could not explain why the characters had made their choices. The next day they tried a different approach: they completed one story carefully, discussed the Qur’anic lesson, and carried out a small helpful act at home. Akhlaq earned fewer flowers, but he remembered the lesson. Salaam explained that the Qur’an teaches us to think about the quality of our deeds. Akhlaq closed the app feeling satisfied that he had learned something he could actually practise.
missions.question: What is a better way to complete a learning mission?
missions.feedback: Good actions are not measured only by how many points or badges appear.
missions.action: Choose one responsibility and do it carefully, not hurriedly.
missions.reflection: What makes a deed good besides being noticed?
missions.vocabulary: Aḥsanu ‘amalan — best in deeds; ‘Azīz — Mighty; Ghafūr — Forgiving
missions.careNote: Teach references to death sensitively, with parental control; no frightening imagery or spiritual rankings.
missions.review: What Qur’anic teaching guided your choice? How is the Amanpur story different from the original verse’s setting?
